vignette: Kai had always been drawn to the sea, and as a fisherman, he found solace in the rhythmic motion of the waves and the camaraderie of his crew. But it was on land, in a dingy room, that Kai's life took a drastic turn. He was captured by armed men while traveling abroad for work, subjected to days of brutal torture, and left with scars that went far beyond the physical. The memories of those dark days lingered, refusing to be extinguished. When Kai recalled the events, he felt an intense rage coursing through his veins, as if his body was reliving the trauma all over again. He would involuntarily assume the same defensive position, curled up and helpless, just like during the torture. The pain came flooding back too - a searing ache in his joints, a throbbing sensation in his head. It was as if no time had passed at all. As Kai navigated his daily life, he found himself becoming increasingly vigilant. He couldn't shake off the feeling of being watched or ambushed. Whenever he rode the bus to work, he'd sit near the driver, eyes scanning the other passengers for potential threats. Babies' cries, in particular, made him jumpy - their wails seemed to echo through his mind like a siren warning of impending danger. Kai couldn't explain why babies triggered this response; all he knew was that it made him want to flee or hide. His wife, Sophia, had given birth to their first child just a few months prior, and while Kai adored being a father, the constant crying and vulnerability of his infant son left him on edge. He began avoiding family gatherings, not wanting to be around when the baby got fussy. Feeling emotionally vulnerable was another trigger for Kai's anxiety. When Sophia tried to talk to him about their relationship or finances, he'd shut down, feeling overwhelmed by the prospect of opening up. "I just can't do this right now," he'd say, turning away from her and escaping into his own world. Kai started taking measures to feel safer in his environment. At home, he'd position himself with his back against a wall, scanning the room for potential escape routes or hiding spots. He'd listen intently for any unusual sounds - creaks, footsteps, whispers - convinced that someone might be lurking outside. His friends and family began noticing these quirks, but Kai couldn't explain them; all he knew was that it made him feel slightly more secure. One day, while working on his fishing boat, Kai spotted a coiled rope near the stern. In an instant, he envisioned using it as a makeshift noose or a whip - just like his captors had done. The sudden image sent a shiver down his spine, and for a moment, he forgot where he was. His crewmates noticed his distraction but said nothing. Sophia finally sat Kai down, her voice laced with concern, "You can't keep living like this, Kai. You're always on edge, always expecting something bad to happen. Our son needs a father who's present, not constantly looking over his shoulder." The words stung, and for the first time, Kai realized that he wasn't just fighting his own demons; he was also risking the well-being of those he loved. It was then that Kai knew he needed help - not just to cope with the memories but to reclaim his life from the shadows of torture. As he sat in the therapist's office, fidgeting with his hands, he whispered, "I don't want to be a prisoner of my own mind anymore."
